hook_text: This lump of coal holds sunshine from before the dinosaurs.
clip_script: eMalahleni: the place of coal. On the table: coal, firewood, paraffin, a gas canister, a candle and a packet of peanuts. Every one is a fuel, a material with stored energy. Burn it, and out comes heat and light. Even the peanuts: one peanut on a pin burns for about a minute! Your body uses food as fuel too. And the energy in coal? Swamp plants caught it from the Sun hundreds of millions of years ago.
visual_style: Whiteboard table of fuels, then a time-travel arrow from a lump of coal back to an ancient swamp forest under the Sun.
mood: Wonder and time travel, like opening an ancient treasure chest.
pacing: Table of fuels, the peanut surprise, then the long journey back to the Sun.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the kilojoules on three food labels at home.
